newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amic's Mondi Europe plans $312 mln rejig.
newsitem.headline: Amic's Mondi Europe plans $312 mln rejig.

text.p: Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd's (Amic) Mondi Europe unit plans a $312 million restructuring and expansion programme which would enlarge and strengthen its pulp, paper and packaging interests, Amic said in a joint statement with other key shareholders on Thursday.

The statement said that Amic, which owns 51 percent of Mondi, had reached agreement with Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd on a series of transactions which would introduce Anglo as a shareholder in Mondi.
The transactions are subject to certain conditions, including the finalising of international loan facilities with Mondi's bankers, the statement said.
"It is envisaged that the new structure will be implemented before the end of November, 1996," it added.
Mondo Europe will be renamed Mondi Minorco Paper.

In terms of the agreement, Mondi and Anglo will inject into Mondi Europe 28 percent of the voting stock of Aracruz Celulose SA and about $62 million in cash to fund an increase in the capital of Frantschach AG.

Mondi's interest in Mondi Europe would rise to 20 percent from its current five percent. Anglo would acquire a 20 percent interest in Mondi Europe with the remaining 60 percent being held by Minorco SA.
Mondi's increased interest would be financed through international loans to be raised for this purpose.
The Frantschach capital increase would increase Mondi Europe's joint controlling interest in Frantschach to 50 percent from 44.4 percent.
According to the statement, the enlarged Mondi Europe would consist of the following jointly controlled investments in the paper, pulp, packaging and related industries:
- 49 percent direct and 25.5 percent indirect interest in Neusiedler AG;

- 50 percent interest in the Frantschach Group. Frantschach has a 51 percent interest in Neusiedler, 40 percent of Bischof & Klein, 55 percent of Europapier and 93 percent of the Pols pulp mill in Austria;
- 28 percent voting (12 percent equity) investment in Aracruz Celulose.
The statement said that the attributable turnover of Mondi Europe was expected to be about $900 million.
Mondi Europe contributed $36.6 million to Minorco's operating earnings in the first half of 1996.
